Question: Is there a documented test strategy per product/service, reviewed at least yearly?
Is test scope/depth explicitly risk-based (tiered), rather than uniform across all features?
Are non-functional requirements (perf, security, a11y) captured at planning time, not discovered late?
Is testability considered during requirements/design review (shift-left)?
Are test estimates/effort tracked against actuals to improve future planning?
Is there a defined process for scoping regression impact when a change is made?
Are non-functional requirements captured as quantified, testable thresholds rather than qualitative statements ("should be fast")?
Is there a defined approval matrix specifying which stakeholders must sign off which test artefacts?
Are test cases derived from documented, traceable requirements/acceptance criteria?
Is there a living test case repository organised by module/component with a consistent naming and tagging scheme?
Are test design techniques (equivalence partitioning, boundary value, state transition, etc.) applied deliberately for complex logic?
Is requirements-to-test traceability tracked and reportable, generated from the tool rather than hand-maintained?
Are test cases reviewed by a peer before being trusted as regression coverage?
Is test case priority risk-based (P0-P3), driven by business criticality, defect hotspots, and usage data?
Is there a scheduled test case health audit (staleness, duplication, re-prioritisation)?
Can traceability be navigated in both directions - story to defect and defect to story?
Is there a reuse-first rule enforced before authoring new test cases (Master Test Pack)?
Is test execution status visible on a live dashboard (not a manually compiled status email)?
Are entry/exit criteria enforced, not just documented?
Is defect triage a scheduled, cross-functional ritual?
Are release sign-off decisions based on objective exit-criteria data?
Is there a retrospective after every release/major defect escape to capture lessons?
Are sprint-package and release-package sign-offs documented records (named approver, role, date, version, conditions)?
Unit testing - minimum expectation met per Testing-Types-Standards.md?
Component/Integration testing - minimum expectation met?
API testing - minimum expectation met?
System/End-to-End testing - minimum expectation met?
Regression testing - minimum expectation met?
Performance testing - minimum expectation met?
Security (SAST/DAST/SCA) testing - minimum expectation met?
Accessibility testing - minimum expectation met?
Usability/UAT - minimum expectation met?
Exploratory testing - minimum expectation met?
Contract testing - minimum expectation met?
Chaos/Resilience testing - minimum expectation met?
Data/ETL testing - minimum expectation met?
Mobile (device/OS matrix) testing - minimum expectation met?
Compatibility (browser/OS) testing - minimum expectation met?
Localization testing - minimum expectation met?
Visual Regression testing - minimum expectation met?
Is there a single defect-tracking source of truth used consistently?
Does defect handling distinguish discovery stage (in-sprint / later-sprint / UAT / production)?
Are severity and priority tracked as two distinct axes with clear owners?
Is there an expedited hotfix path for production-Critical defects?
Are defects root-caused, with recurring patterns analysed?
Is escaped-defect analysis fed back into test design with a concrete resulting change?
Are defect SLAs (by severity) defined and tracked?
Are non-functional defects classified on their domain-specific scale and routed correctly, with security findings access-restricted?
Are known issues risk-accepted for release added to the product backlog and reviewed on a defined cadence?
Are test environments provisioned via self-service/IaC rather than manual ticketing?
Is environment-to-production parity tracked and drift alerted?
Is there a dedicated performance environment with a documented prod-parity/scaling-extrapolation model?
Does recurring environment instability trigger a formal root-cause investigation?
Is test data synthetic/masked with no raw PII in non-prod, and is masking validated by an automated scan on every refresh?
Is sanitized production data refreshed into non-prod on a defined, followed cadence?
Is test data refresh/reset self-service and fast enough to not block testers?
Is there a standardised automation framework (not ad hoc per-engineer style)?
Is automated test code version-controlled and code-reviewed like production code?
Is flaky-test management a full lifecycle (detect -> quarantine -> SLA root-cause -> re-admission)?
Is the automation pyramid respected (majority unit/API, thin E2E layer)?
Is there a documented, agreed set of criteria for what must be automated in-sprint vs. deferred?
Does automation run on every PR/commit?
Can the automated suite gate a merge/deploy?
Is execution parallelised/distributed to keep feedback time short?
Is there dedicated capacity (SDET role/time) for automation maintenance?
Is in-sprint automation the default target, with deviation tracked as prioritised technical debt?
Is there protected sprint/PI capacity (10-20%) for automation maintenance/upskilling, with delivery tracked?
Does each suite tier run at a defined frequency/environment/pipeline stage, with health judged from a stable environment?
Is the team's tool stack within the org's approved categories?
Is tooling choice justified by need rather than individual preference/legacy inertia?
Is tool usage/licensing tracked for cost governance?
Is there integration between tools rather than manual data re-entry?
Is AI used anywhere in the test lifecycle?
Is AI usage through an org-approved/governed tool with human review before artefacts are trusted?
Is the impact of AI usage measured (time saved, quality uplift)?
Is there awareness/training on AI risks (hallucination, data leakage)?
Is there a defined skills/competency matrix for testers/SDETs?
Are individual development plans tied to identified skill gaps?
Is there a career path for testers into SDET/QE leadership?
Is knowledge-sharing (brown bags, wiki, community of practice) active?
Is tester competency reassessed on a defined cadence against a documented rubric, with upskill progress tracked?
Are the org-standard KPIs tracked for this team?
Is there a quarterly maturity self-assessment/re-assessment rhythm already in place?
Are improvement actions from the last assessment tracked to closure?
Is quality treated as a whole-team responsibility, not siloed to a QA team?
Do Product/Business stakeholders participate in UAT/acceptance reviews?
Is there psychological safety to raise a quality concern and delay a release?
Is testing represented in sprint/release planning as first-class work?
Does a tester participate in backlog refinement to review AC testability?
Is test approach/estimate discussed alongside dev estimate at sprint planning?
Do testers raise blockers in standup as first-class impediments?
Is there an explicit, scheduled feature-level aggregation test pass before a feature is declared Done?
Is there a feature-level demo/showcase distinct from the routine sprint-level demo?
Does the retrospective carry a standing quality question?
Is release cadence explicitly declared, with every release passing a pre-production gate?
Does regression scope for a release scale with the number of sprints' worth of change batched into it?
